# hc-teleport

Run `hc-teleport <machine> --detach` once with your shell tool, from this session's own terminal. The machine is the one the person named. If no machine is named, ask which, and offer the machines `hc-teleport doctor` lists. Add `--wait <seconds>` only if the person asks for a longer wait for the session to go idle.

Then end the turn at once. The move starts only when this session is idle, so never wait, poll or run `hc-teleport status` in this turn.

If the command refuses, tell the person and stop:

- `not_initialized`: run `hc-teleport init` in a terminal (the wizard is interactive), then try again.
- `machine_not_allowed`: the machine, named in the message, is not allowed; run `hc-teleport init` in a terminal to allow it.
- `move_in_progress`: a move of this session is already running; see `hc-teleport status`.
- `not_in_a_terminal`: this session does not run in an hc terminal.
- `not_claude`: only Claude Code sessions move today, and this agent's sessions cannot move yet.

# hc-teleport-agent

Gives OpenCode and Pi a `/hc-teleport <machine>` command and the `hc-teleport` skill. Both tell the agent to run `hc-teleport <machine> --detach` once and end its turn, so the session moves once it is idle. The CLI moves only Claude Code sessions today: for any other agent it refuses with `not_claude`, and the agent tells the person its sessions cannot move yet. The `hc-teleport` CLI must be installed on the machine; see https://github.com/ejklock/hc-teleport.

## OpenCode

Add the package to `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["hc-teleport-agent"] }
```

Its `config` hook adds the skill and the `hc-teleport` command. An `hc-teleport` command you define yourself wins.

## Pi

```
pi install npm:hc-teleport-agent
```

Pi then loads the `hc-teleport` skill and the `/hc-teleport` prompt template.
